thread:
pagerbot: [SECURITY] Unusual auth-probe detected on edge-proxy x-edge-01. Multiple PUTs to S3 from svcacct-ingest; pattern matches automated log-forwarding. Severity: P0-security. Investigate immediate containment.

Anna (oncall): taking it. @Sam can you confirm whether S3 forwarding was intentionally configured? @Lia please join for classification. I'll spin up a bridge.

Sam (ops): on it. tailing edge logs now ->
```
$ sudo tail -n 200 /var/log/edge-proxy/access.log | grep PUT | grep staging-logs
2026-03-17T12:05:21 PUT /logs svcacct-ingest 10.12.3.45 "curl/7.82"
2026-03-17T12:05:23 PUT /logs svcacct-ingest 10.12.3.46 "curl/7.82"
2026-03-17T12:05:27 PUT /logs svcacct-ingest 10.12.3.47 "curl/7.82"
```
43 PUTs in last 4m. IPs grouped in two ASNs. Not normal.

Lia (sec): this looks like scripted exfil. Likely service account creds abused. Recommend: 1) Immediately revoke svcacct-ingest write keys, 2) remove bucket write ACLs to staging-logs-backup, 3) identify destination buckets. @Ben start key rotation now.

Ben (infra): starting rotation. Steps I'm running:
1) Disable current keys for svcacct-ingest in IAM.
2) Create new key pair, encrypt with KMS, write to vault.
3) Deploy new secret to ingest fleet with rolling restart.
ETA ~20m. Running: `aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIA... --status Inactive --user-name svcacct-ingest`

Maria (support): any customer impact yet? We have one live ticket about delayed logs (CS-12345). If we have to cut writes for staging-logs-backup, that may delay delivery. I'll prep a short notification.

Anna (oncall): bridge created by bridgebot -> https://zoom.company/incident-7301234567 (bridge pinned). @Legal notified as well. Lia, can you confirm if any PII in recent uploads?

bridgebot: Incident bridge started by Anna. Link above. Recorder enabled.

Lia (sec): quick grep of recent PUT payloads (sampled) shows plaintext debug dumps with request_ids and truncated user identifiers. Possible PII. Marking as potential privacy event. Escalating to Legal.

Legal: acknowledged. Please preserve evidence and add findings to the incident tracker (privacy flag). Do NOT delete any objects until we confirm export timeline.

Ben (infra): old key disabled. Created new key and injected into vault. Pushing secret rotation to 4 ingestion nodes now: `vault write secret/ingest svc_key=XXX && kubectl rollout restart ds/ingest-service`

Sam (ops): I changed S3 bucket policy to block writes from svcacct-ingest principal while we rotate: `aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket staging-logs-backup --policy file://deny-svcacct-put.json` (policy denies PutObject for that principal). Observed PUTs drop to zero after change.

Lia (sec): found destination bucket temp-uploads-9f3 in same account that recently received objects matching our pattern. Listing recent objects and locking bucket for further writes.

Ben (infra): revoked keys associated with temp-uploads pipeline too. KMS logs show new key usage after rotation, will verify. Rolling back access for any service principals that have write perms unrelated to ingestion.

Anna (oncall): good containment. Next: 1) full object inventory for temp-uploads-9f3, 2) preserve objects for forensic review, 3) coordinate customer comms if PII confirmed, 4) rotate any downstream keys that had access. Assign tasks?

Sam (ops): doing object inventory now -> `aws s3 ls s3://temp-uploads-9f3 --recursive --human-readable --summarize` scraping metadata to incident bucket.

Maria (support): preparing templated customer note. Will wait for Lia/Legal on PII confirmation before sending.

Lia (sec): preliminary sample indicates user identifiers and trace IDs, some email hashes. Marking as "suspected data exposure". Recommend notifying affected customers within SLA.

Legal: we'll prepare notification guidance. Please attach list of object keys and timestamps to the ticket. Avoid stating certainty until forensics complete.

Ben (infra): rotation complete across ingestion fleet. New keys in vault, nodes restarted. Monitoring for failed writes or auth errors.

Sam (ops): edge logs show no new PUT spikes in the last 10m. Network scans show the 3 source IPs now offline.

Anna (oncall): OK. Summary for incident: automated auth-probe exploited svcacct-ingest creds to PUT logs into secondary bucket. Containment: keys rotated, bucket write blocked, temp-uploads-9f3 write blocked and objects preserved. Action items: forensics (Lia), customer comms (Maria + Legal), postmortem + runbook updates (Anna).

Lia (sec): saving evidence to secure bucket and starting deeper analysis. Will report ETA 2h.

Ben (infra): thumbs up. I'll follow up with a sudo-runbook patch to prevent overly permissive service accounts.

Anna (oncall): handing off active mitigation to Lia/Ben. I'll remain on-call for coordination. Closing handover in 10m if no regressions. :lock: :white_check_mark:

pagerbot: Update: incident severity downgraded to P1 after containment. Continue monitoring.

Anna (oncall): last check — no new PUTs for 25m, no customer complaints beyond CS-12345. Keeping incident open until forensics complete.

bridgebot: Recorder stopped. Meeting notes saved to incident-7301234567 in Drive.

Lia (sec): forensic snapshot saved. Moving to analysis phase. Will post initial report.

Maria (support): drafted customer note ready for Legal review.

Anna (oncall): thanks all. Stand down for active paging; please update the incident tracker with final notes when done.
